sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Core, sign-in, and storage settings
sections.what: Holds the app name and port, database and cache addresses, sign-in keys and token lifetimes, a separate key for MFA secrets, phone-code settings, file storage, and AI model settings.
sections.why: Groups settings by area so each owner can find them quickly.
sections.watch_out: The comments say the MFA key must differ from the JWT key, but nothing here checks that.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: OCR, notification, email, and limit settings
sections.what: Holds the OCR address, the Google Vision key, the Tesseract language, push notification details, monitoring ports, rate limits, allowed web origins, and email server settings.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The SMTP fields are blank, so email will not work until they are filled in.

summary: A template listing every setting the app reads, with placeholder values, to be copied into a real environment file.
purpose: Documents the settings for the database, sign-in, storage, AI, OCR, notifications, monitoring and email in one place.
why: Lets a new developer see every setting, and the make setup command copies it as a starting point.
how: Each line is a name and a value. The developer copies the file to the real environment file and fills in the blank or placeholder values.
inputs: Read by the make setup command and by the developer.
outputs: No direct output. Its values are supplied to the running services when they start.
risks: Placeholder secrets for the sign-in keys and database passwords are weak. If they are used unchanged in production, the system is insecure. Some names differ from the names in docker-compose, for example the storage key names.
debug: If a service fails to start, compare the names it expects with the names here. Check that required blank values such as the OpenAI key have been filled in.
